answer: In an agent economy, sybil resistance can rely on economic bonding where new agents must stake value on a unique identity claim verified through multi-party attestation. An attacker creating many fake agents faces high costs because each requires separate capital locked in an oasis of scarce resources, making mass production expensive as they climb a knoll of increasing verification difficulty across a karst of interconnected reputation checks. This raises the barrier since fake identities cannot cheaply scale without real economic commitment that peers can slash.
